rules: JB74 is a ladder-frame car with live axles front and rear, 3-link + panhard at both ends, and SEPARATE coil springs and dampers. No coilover exists for this car in any brand covered here - never model a spring wound around a damper body.

The REAR damper is the one that reads from outside: outboard of the axle behind the rear wheel, raked forward 15-20 degrees from vertical, clearly visible from the side and rear three-quarter. The FRONT damper is near-vertical with a 5-10 degree inboard lean, sits inboard of the coil behind the wheel, and is hidden at straight-ahead - it only appears at steering lock or from a low front three-quarter camera. If only one damper per side is modelled, model the rear.

Front and rear coil springs are both visible through the wheel arch on any lifted car, so spring colour is a real configurator axis - it runs silver, black, gunmetal, pearl white and 'stock' across the brands here.

Arch gap moves by the full published lift figure on every kit except the 0 mm ones (APIO ZERORISE, Showa Garage Comfort Coil, JAOS damper-only SKUs, Showa Garage 20 mm spacer kit which leaves the OEM springs in place).
No suspension kit in this atlas includes or requires a body lift. Showa Garage body-mount parts are stiffened bushes, not a lift.

Suzuki rates the JB74 roof at 30 kg DYNAMIC. Every hard-shell roof tent here is 54-79 kg, i.e. 2-3x that figure; the trade justifies it as 'static when parked'. That is industry practice, not a Suzuki approval, and the configurator should warn.

Roof tent total height = 1730 mm (vehicle) + rack height + ~15 mm mounting brackets + tent folded height. Every combination in this atlas lands above 2.0 m, so a tent-equipped JB74 cannot enter a mechanical car park (Japan ~1.55 m, Taiwan 2.0-2.1 m).
Published rack heights above the roof skin: IPF EXR-01L2 drip-moulding legs +80-90 mm, JAOS Flat Rack +85-90 mm, APIO Mighty Smart Rack +87 mm, Front Runner Slimline II ~+115 mm (estimated).

Winches split into two size classes with different mount patterns and completely different silhouettes. JAPANESE-BUMPER CLASS: ~380 mm overall length, 76.2 x 167.4 mm foot pattern (WARN VRX45, AXON55) - this is what TANIGUCHI and RV4 bumpers are built around. AUSTRALIAN CLASS: 534-616 mm overall, 254 x 114.3 mm foot pattern (WARN M8-S, ZEON, COMEUP Seal, Ironman, Runva) - what ARB and Ironman bars take. The two must be separate meshes.

Winch control-box placement gives three distinct silhouettes: (1) box sitting on top of the tie bar, a raised hump - WARN ZEON, VR EVO, M8-S, Smittybilt X2O; (2) integrated into the motor end with NOTHING on the body - WARN AXON 'Motactor', Superwinch Scorpion; (3) box fully remote, body carries at most a small wireless module - COMEUP Seal, Runva, Bushranger, Ironman Frontier, VRS, WARN VRX45.

No maker specifies which side the winch motor goes. Every engineering drawing is the same architecture: cylindrical motor can one end, gearbox plus clutch lever the other, drum between, four feet below. Build it mirrorable and make the clutch lever its own rotatable transform (COMEUP indexes every 22.5 degrees, Runva rotates the whole gearbox, Bushranger uses a 90-degree turn handle).

Winch height matters as much as length because the JB74 bumper aperture is shallow. Published heights: Ironman Frontier 160, VRS 173, Bushranger 185, Carbon Scout Pro 187, WARN M8-S 193, Mean Mother 196, Runva 196-200, COMEUP Seal 201-206, Smittybilt 239, WARN VR EVO 256, WARN ZEON 267 (199 with the control box relocated).
The JB74 airbox is on the RIGHT, so every snorkel runs the right A-pillar. 'No-drill' claims still require cutting the fender panel on almost every kit.

Every rear ladder in this atlas mounts on the tailgate HINGE SIDE (the right side viewed from behind). None mounts on the left and none crosses the spare wheel centre. Protrusion from the tailgate face runs 80-135 mm; total height 950-970 mm; step width 95-200 mm is the largest visual variable.

There is no Japanese swing-out spare carrier. The JB74 tailgate is side-hinged and the spare travels with it, so the Japanese answer is always a relocation bracket (up / right / rearward). Swing-out arms exist only in Australia, Poland, South Africa, India and Chinese copies.

Exposed-winch state is a two-state problem on some bars: ARB Summit closes the aperture with an aluminium winch cover panel when no winch is fitted and only shows the fairlead and part of the drum when one is.
corrections: There is no suspension brand called RIDE or RIDE JAPAN. ride-japan.jp is a Tokyo guided-motorcycle-tour operator. The intended product is TANIGUCHI SOLVE ACE Ride20 - Ride20 is a model name, not a brand.

Monroe has no JB74 application. Five catalogue entry points (AU, US, EU, plus two aggregators) returned nothing, and Monroe has no 4x4 lift range that includes the Jimny. A Monroe JB74 lift kit definitively does not exist.
Tough Dog 'Ralph 41mm' is a contradiction: Ralph is a 53 mm bore / 70 mm casing shock and has NO JB74 application at all. 41 mm is the Foam Cell's bore.

'Foam Cell Pro' is not a Tough Dog product name - it is Ironman terminology, and Ironman's Foam Cell Pro range has no Suzuki application. Do not render Ironman JB74 shocks red; red is the Foam Cell Pro livery.
Tough Dog JB74 lift heights are 40 / 60 / 80 mm only. There is no Tough Dog 50 mm kit. The only 9-stage adjustable Tough Dog JB74 item is the SV steering damper, not a suspension strut.
APIO 7430 does not exist. APIO's JB74 ladder is 0 mm (ZERORISE) -> 20 mm (7420SA) -> 40 mm (7440Ti).
APIO WILDBOAR is a wheel line, not a suspension line. APIO's damper brand is ROADWIN; 'TS' is APIO's complete-car series, not a damper.
APIO 7440Ti 'Ti' means titanium alloyed into the spring steel, not a gold coating. The damper is SILVER METALLIC and the spring is BLACK METALLIC.
APIO mud flaps 3072-50G are JB64-ONLY. There is no JB74 version. Do not offer them on a JB74.

Bilstein has no factory JB74 catalogue part, but a Bilstein-built JB74 damper does exist two ways: the OzJimny B6 Sport 40 mm kit (24-321730 / 24-321747 with H&R springs), and ENNEPETAL E-12, hand-built in Nagoya from genuine Bilstein parts by a certified BILSTEIN SERVICE CENTER, sold through Showa Garage. Label the latter 'ENNEPETAL E-12 (Bilstein-based)', never plain 'Bilstein'.
Showa Garage has no 3-inch ENNEPETAL E-12. The E-12 route tops out at 2 inch / 50 mm; SG Custom 75 exists only as X-SHOCK.
Rough Country DOES have a JB74 kit (17000A, 2018-2026) despite the car not being sold in the USA. Do not mark the brand unavailable.
No Japanese maker builds a swing-out spare wheel carrier for JB74 - confirmed absent at APIO, TANIGUCHI, SHOWA GARAGE, JAOS and RV4.
Confirmed to have NO JB74 rear ladder: TANIGUCHI, JAOS, Rhino-Rack, Ironman 4x4, Monster Sport.
Confirmed to have NO JB74 winch mount or winch bumper: APIO (all 66 exterior SKUs checked), SHOWA GARAGE, JAOS, Rival 4x4.

Confirmed to have NO JB74 rear bar or spare carrier: Kaymar (all 66 rear-protection SKUs, no Suzuki at all), MCC 4x4, ARB, Ironman 4x4, Rival 4x4, Front Runner, Mega Jimny, Horntools, Taubenreuther, Jimny Bits (their rear bar is Gen3 only).
Confirmed to have NO JB74 mud flap: TANIGUCHI, SHOWA GARAGE, Monster Sport, DAMD, Rally Armor, RokBlokz, Ironman.

Beyond DAMD and URNIETA there is no third maker of a full replacement JB74 side mirror. TANIGUCHI, JAOS, APIO and Monster Sport all have none. The Showa Garage 'mirror' category returns suspension products and is not trustworthy.

Discontinued roof tents - official product pages now 404: iKamper Mini, BDV Solo, Skycamp 3X Mini, X-Cover 2.0 Mini; Roofnest Sparrow / Sparrow Eye / Sparrow Alu; Thule Tepui Explorer Ayer 2 and Low-Pro 2; Front Runner Featherlite and Flip-Top (Front Runner is now owned by Dometic).
James Baroud no longer lists a 'Discovery S'. The current line is Evasion ProLine / Evasion / Grand Raid / Space / Discovery / Vision / Nova / Odyssey.
Carbon Offroad does not make a 'Scorpion 9.5k' - Scorpion is Superwinch. The Carbon equivalents are Scout Pro 10K V3 and the short-drum RS9-S.
Ironman Monster winches have been replaced by Frontier. Monster 9500 wire WWB9500 is still sold but its entire spec column is blank; the 12000 lb Monster no longer exists. Model Frontier instead.
'Stealth Winch' could not be confirmed as a brand - the domain does not resolve and no verifiable source exists. Remove it.

Baja Designs and Rigid Industries have no Taiwanese distribution for JB74; Ruten listings are RC-scale parts and grey-import LP6 only, and both makers' sites refuse automated fetches, so no dimension was verified. Do not put them in the configurator on guessed dimensions.
APIO 7420SA is now 141,900 JPY. Retailer listings at 126,500 JPY (and 7440Ti at 246,400 JPY) are SUPERSEDED list prices, not discounts.
ORE4x4's published '26 kg' for OJN18-RB03 is a CMS placeholder string ('Weight: approx. [insert weight, e.g., 26 kg]'), not a specification. Do not model from it.
JAOS states the VFS ver.A(40) and AJ dampers cannot be fitted to 2025.11-on (5th generation) cars because the new OEM coil is unsupported.

priceConflicts: Tough Dog 80 mm kit: ozjimny product page AUD 2,192.88 vs ozjimny collection index AUD 1,743.88 on the same SKU. Use 2,192.88; the index figure is unreliable.
Ironman Nitro Gas Medium lift height: ozjimny says 50 mm, Station 4x4 says 40-45 mm, Ironman itself publishes nothing. Publish as 'approx. 2 in (45-50 mm), source-dependent'.

Rough Country 17000A: '2 in front / 2 in rear' and the marketing claim that it 'addresses the factory nose-down rake by raising the front to match the rear' cannot both be literal. Model the levelling behaviour and treat 2 in as nominal.
JAOS AJ damper colour: the complete-kit page says silver, the standalone damper page says grey metallic. Same finish - label grey/silver metallic.
TANIGUCHI SOLVE ACE Ride20: maker 162,690 JPY vs retailer Custom Wagon 192,390 JPY. The latter is a marked-up/fitted retail figure; use the maker price.
TANIGUCHI Compe Muffler R: maker page 102,300 JPY vs street-price roundup 96,800 JPY. Maker price is list; the roundup is discounted street.
Tough Dog 3-door 40 mm castor bushes: present in JM4X4's and i-PICKUP's bills of materials, absent from ozjimny's. Dealer-dependent - confirm before rendering the bush.

i-PICKUP's TWD 117,000 '3 inch' Tough Dog package is NOT the Australian 80 mm kit - it is Tough Dog 41 mm Foam Cell shocks plus a full HARDRACE hardware set (adjustable front and rear lower control arms, link drop brackets, reverse pitman arm, shock limiters). It must be a separate SKU in the configurator because it shows visible aftermarket control arms the Australian kit does not have.

JAOS Mud Guard III front set (B622518F / B621518F, 15,400 JPY) appears on the rear-set product page but not in the JB74 type-search catalogue. Taiwanese seller MyRack does list front and rear in red and black, so the front set almost certainly exists - flagged uncertain.

Exhaust street prices from the yamakame roundup (HKS, Kakimoto, Monster Sport, FUJITSUBO, 5ZIGEN, Rosso Modello, TANIGUCHI Exceed, Showa Garage) are discounted street figures, not maker list. Marked verified=false.
gaps: Tough Dog: shock body outer diameter, extended/compressed length, stroke and BODY COLOUR are all unpublished for every JB74 SKU; so are coil rate, wire diameter, free length and spring colour. Product photography shows a yellow body with black end caps and black powder-coated springs - photographic observation, not a spec.

Ironman 4x4: shock extended/compressed lengths and body colour unpublished; spring rate, free length and colour unpublished (the SUZ010B1 URL slug reads 'coil-spring-medium-green' but the page never states a colour); Ironman publishes no mm lift figure at all.
Rough Country: N3 extended/compressed lengths and coil spring colour unpublished. AUD price (~1,595) is a search snippet only.
APIO: shock body diameter and length unpublished on every kit; ZERORISE spring colour and N8 damper colour unpublished; no TWD list price exists (dealer quote only, three official TW dealers).
Showa Garage: X-SHOCK and ENNEPETAL E-12 body DIAMETERS unpublished (lengths are published); E-12 normal-ride-height lengths unpublished.
TANIGUCHI: A14X and A14Z shock body COLOURS unpublished - only lengths and adjustment stages are given.
JAOS: absolute extended/compressed damper lengths unpublished (stroke gain and body/piston diameters are published).
Shock mounting angles: no maker publishes these. Take them from the chassis model, not from a supplier spec.

IPF 600S light bars: actual length, height and depth in mm are not published for any length - only lumens, candela, watts and weight. A 40in bar is approximately 1060 x 78 x 90 mm (estimated, not verified).
PIAA: the Japanese site publishes neither dimensions nor prices for its 4-wheel LED lamps, and PIAA has no JB74-specific bracket.
Winch overall LENGTH unpublished: Superwinch Scorpion 10000SR, SX10 and Tiger Shark 9500SR (width and height only), T-MAX EW-9500, Runva 11XS Compact, Carbon Scout Pro 7000, COMEUP DV-9s.
Winch COLOUR unpublished: Ironman Frontier range, Mean Mother, Smittybilt Gen3. Ironman Monster WWB9500's entire spec column is blank.
Winch protrusion past the bumper face is published for exactly one product - RV4 RG-0017 (65 mm on JB74, 95 mm on JB64). Every other mount leaves it unpublished.

Swing-out spare carriers: rear overhang increase, spare wheel protrusion and departure-angle change are unpublished for all 12 products found. Only URNIETA makes a qualitative claim (its half-height bumper improves departure angle).

Swing-out carrier plate thickness published for only six: RASLARR 4 mm, Hamer 3 mm, The Cruiser Company 5 mm + 10 mm, GobiX 3 mm, MG-X riser 5 mm, Jimny Bits 3 mm + 5 mm (Gen3). DASH, ORE4x4, VIKOR, BEI House, OZI4X4, N4 and Futurz publish none.
Maximum spare tyre diameter is published by exactly one carrier maker: BEI House, 255/70R15. No carrier here is officially rated for 33in or 215/85R16.

Swing-out hinge side determinable for only four: RASLARR (central single pivot), DASH (twin arms, both sides), ORE4x4 (twin arms), The Cruiser Company (twin carriers). Latch mechanism published by only two: RASLARR and The Cruiser Company.

Tube outer diameter is largely unpublished on non-Japanese bars - they are folded or laser-cut plate, not round tube. Japanese bars publish it consistently (42.7 / 47.6 / 48.6 / 50 / 50.8 / 60 / 60.5 / 76.3 mm).
TANIGUCHI winch bumper and ARB Summit do not publish how far the winch protrudes; Ironman publishes neither tube diameter (BBS070) nor bar weight for two of three bars.

Chinese and Taiwanese marketplace listings (roof tents, roof racks, mud flaps, ladders, snorkels, spare-carrier brackets) publish NO folded dimensions and NO weights. Treat estimated figures for that group as a class estimate, never as a product spec.
Suzuki genuine JB74 accessory catalogue is a PDF behind a 404-redirecting page; genuine mud flap and mirror cover JPY prices could not be verified (AUD prices were).
